**Clinical Summary:**  
A patient presents with a 3-month history of progressive gait impairment requiring wheelchair use, preceded by 1-year duration of urinary incontinence and accompanied by recent-onset slurred speech (dysarthria). No numbness, tingling, objective weakness, or imbalance reported.

Other mimics (e.g., vitamin deficiencies, Wilson’s disease, autoimmune encephalitis, structural myelopathy) are effectively excluded by laboratory and imaging data. - Recent-onset slurred speech (dysarthria) — a brainstem/cerebellar sign commonly seen in MSA-C.  
- Brain MRI shows multifocal atrophy and signal abnormalities in brainstem, cerebellum, and basal ganglia — hallmark neuroimaging pattern of MSA (e.g., hot cross bun sign, putaminal rim hyperintensity, pontine atrophy).

- Negative anti-GAD65 antibody — makes autoimmune cerebellar ataxia less likely.  
- No reported numbness, tingling, or objective weakness — argues against peripheral neuropathy, dorsal column disease, or myelopathy.

[GAPS]  
- Absence of documented orthostatic hypotension (blood pressure measurements supine vs. standing not reported).  
- No formal assessment of parkinsonism (e.g., bradykinesia, rigidity, rest tremor) or cerebellar signs (e.g., limb ataxia, nystagmus, oculomotor deficits).

- Sleep history (e.g., REM sleep behavior disorder) and laryngeal exam (e.g., stridor) not documented — both supportive features of MSA.

[DIAGNOSIS]  
Multiple system atrophy, cerebellar type (MSA-C)
